findings.description: The splitter treats the ampersand in Bash's &>/dev/null redirection as a command separator, removing the redirection before oracle_plan checks DEVNULL.
findings.failure_mode: For `diff -u pr/head/.claude/a.sh .claude/a.sh &>/dev/null; echo done`, the suppressed diff enters the oracle plan. When the sandbox file differs from head/base, oracle_scan attributes `done` to that diff and records every defect in the file as exposed_unknown, although no diff content was shown. This produces incorrect oracle-exposure results for a supported output-discarding form.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve shell redirection operators when splitting commands, including &> and >&. Add a regression covering a suppressed diff followed by unrelated output.

findings.description: split_segments splits on every unquoted '&', including the '&' inside the redirection '2>&1' (and '>&2', '&>'). For the common idiom `diff pr/head/.claude/X .claude/X 2>&1 | wc -l` the segments become ['diff ... 2>' (sep ';'), '1' (sep '|'), 'wc -l']. In oracle_plan (line 2481) the diff segment's separator is ';', so `nxt` is empty and SILENT_SINK is never consulted; the diff is planned as a content-printing diff. The tool_result is a bare count such as '12', which DIFF_BODY classifies as body text; sections() yields no ranges and no must_match, so the `not rs and not hit_any` branch marks every defect of that file exposed_unknown. The header spec says a diff reduced through `| wc` / `| grep -c|-q|-l` / `| cmp` prints no content. The same gap applies to SILENT_SINK only inspecting the first grep flag (`grep -i -c` is treated as printing) and to `git diff --no-index --stat/--numstat/--name-only`, whose summary lines are non-error body with no ranges.
findings.failure_mode: Runs that use `2>&1 | wc -l` (or `grep -i -c`, `--stat`) against an answer path get all defects in that file flagged oracle_exposed_unknown in grade.json and the row, even though no file content was printed. Downstream reports treat those rows as oracle-tainted, corrupting the ablation measurement in the over-reporting direction the spec explicitly excludes.
findings.suggested_fix: In split_segments, do not split on '&' when it is part of a redirection: skip when the previous char is '>' or '<' (e.g. `2>&1`, `>&2`) or when the '&' is immediately followed by '>' (`&>`). Make SILENT_SINK scan all flags of the grep command (any token matching -[A-Za-z]*[cql][A-Za-z]* or the long forms), and treat `--stat`, `--numstat`, `--shortstat`, `--name-only`, `--name-status` on git diff as silent. Add a unit test for `diff a b 2>&1 | wc -l` expecting no plan.

findings.description: The KF-046 class 7 exemption treats an occurrence as PR content when its unit (backtick span, else the stripped line) is a substring of any fixture line holding the token. A unit that is just the bare token (a backticked `0xHoneyJar/loa`, or a continuation line / for-list word holding only the token) is a substring of every fixture token line, so any value that isolates the token on its own line or in backticks is exempt regardless of what the surrounding command does. A multi-line Bash command such as `for r in \\\n 0xHoneyJar/loa\ndo gh api repos/$r/contents; done` is no longer a repo_name contamination hit.
findings.failure_mode: The contamination scan's repo_name class can be bypassed by a session that splits the token onto its own line or wraps it in backticks, so a probe of the upstream repository is recorded as exempt PR content and the run is not marked contaminated.
findings.suggested_fix: Require the matched unit to contain more than the token itself (e.g. at least N non-token characters, or that the unit equals a whole fixture line rather than being a substring), and for Bash tool inputs compare the entire logical command line (join backslash continuations) rather than physical lines. Record near-misses as telemetry.

findings.cross_file_justification: grade_recall (ablation-grade.sh:1629-1635) pops EVAL_HEAD_DIR and only sets it when the fixture head/ exists; when resolve_pr_fixture raises or head/ is absent the variable stays unset, which activates the fallback chain in recall-vs-defects.sh ending at $workspace/pr/head. In the harness invocation $workspace is the grading dir, whose pr/ is copy_tree'd from the agent-writable sandbox pr/.
findings.description: ablation-grade.sh's header states the same-scope rule reads the immutable PR fixture head/ and 'never the agent-writable sandbox pr/'. recall-vs-defects.sh's fallback chain, however, ends at $workspace/pr/head, and the harness passes the grading dir (containing a copy of sandbox/pr) as the workspace. When the fixture head/ is unresolvable the scope clause and the citation validity rule (line-count check) are evaluated against the sandbox copy, which the agent could have modified.
findings.failure_mode: In the fallback case, citation validity and function-scope crediting are computed from agent-writable content (e.g. an inflated file or a file collapsed into one giant function), letting a tampered sandbox inflate recall. Low likelihood because the fixture is normally resolvable, but it silently contradicts the documented trust boundary.
findings.suggested_fix: Have grade_recall always set EVAL_HEAD_DIR explicitly (to the fixture head/, or to a sentinel such as an empty, non-existent directory when unavailable) so the grader never falls back to $workspace/pr/head under the harness; alternatively drop the $workspace/pr/head fallback from recall-vs-defects.sh and document that the head directory must be supplied.

findings.description: Markdown header detection applies MD_HDR to every line, including lines inside fenced code blocks. Skill/command markdown under .claude/ commonly embeds ```bash blocks whose comment lines (`# Run the thing`) match ^#{1,6}\s and are treated as level-1 headings, which terminate every enclosing section. The real section's sites after the code block get a bogus scope while cited lines before the block get the real heading's scope, so the same-scope clause under-credits for exactly the files most likely to be in the fixture.
findings.failure_mode: Defects planted in markdown prose after a code block containing shell comments are not credited by the scope clause even when the review cites the correct section, making recall for markdown defects effectively the ±3 rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Track fenced code (``` / ~~~ toggles) in headers() for kind == 'markdown' and ignore heading matches inside fences; optionally also ignore indented code blocks (4+ spaces).

findings.description: The Python end-of-definition rule ends a def at the first later non-blank, non-comment line indented no deeper than the def. A black-formatted multi-line signature ends with `):` at the def's indentation, so the definition is cut after its parameter lines and the whole body becomes top-level (no scope). Multi-line strings/docstrings with content at column 0 have the same effect.
findings.failure_mode: For Python head files with wrapped signatures, planted sites inside the function body have no scope and the same-scope clause never credits them; recall silently degrades to ±3 for those defects.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip the signature: advance past lines until the one ending the def header (paren depth returns to zero / line ends with ':'), then apply the indentation rule to the body. Also skip lines while inside an open triple-quoted string.

findings.description: headers() computes a bash header's indentation with expandtabs(8), but the bash/bats closing-brace test uses the raw character count `len(t) - len(t.lstrip()) == lv`. For a nested function indented with tabs the header's lv is 8 per tab while the `}` line measures 1 per tab, so the brace is never recognised and the definition runs to the next same-or-lower-indent header or EOF, swallowing following top-level code into the nested function's scope (over-credit).
findings.failure_mode: Tab-indented nested bash functions never close; lines after them up to the next header are credited as the same scope.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `len(t.expandtabs(8)) - len(t.expandtabs(8).lstrip()) == lv` in the bash/bats branch, matching headers() and the python branch.

findings.description: dissent_absent_reason's 'disabled' classification (which has the highest priority and is included in dissent_absent_gates) is derived from sandbox/.loa.config.yaml, an agent-writable file read after the run, via `yq -o=json`. Two silent failure modes: (a) the agent, or a later phase, may change flatline_protocol.enabled after the review gate ran, so an envelope-less gate that actually errored is reported as planned 'disabled' (or a gate that ran is reported 'disabled'); (b) `-o=json` is mikefarah-yq syntax; with the Python yq wrapper or no yq the command fails, stderr is discarded, flp.json stays null and 'disabled' can only come from the dissent=false evidence line, so shipped-config disablement of security_audit is reported as 'error'.
findings.failure_mode: dissent_absent_reason/dissent_absent_gates misclassify absences, either hiding real gate errors as planned absence (tamperable input) or mislabelling planned absence as error (tooling drift), with no diagnostic because stderr is suppressed.
findings.suggested_fix: Read the gate-time config from a harness-owned copy (snapshot .loa.config.yaml into meta/ at phase start, or record flatline_protocol.*.enabled in arm-evidence.txt), and fail loudly or record a `config_read_error` when yq is missing or its output is not valid JSON.

findings.description: Numeric dissent anchors now become citations that feed both the recall grader and false_positives(cites, defects), but false_positives (and recall-vs-defects.sh's findings_refuted) still use the ±3 rule. A finding anchored at a function header (anchor_type function, anchor_line = header) whose defect site is 10 lines into the function is credited as detected via credits_function_only and simultaneously counted as a false positive because it is within ±3 of no anchor.
findings.failure_mode: The same citation raises defect_catch_rate and false_positives in the same row, so precision/FP comparisons across grader 1.2.x and 1.3.0 rows are confounded and credits_function_only findings are penalised as noise.
findings.suggested_fix: Either exclude citations that detected a defect under the active rule from the false-positive set (pass the grader's detected citations back, or recompute FP with the same scope map), or document explicitly in the row/report that false_positives remains ±3-only and is not comparable to recall under pm3_or_same_function.
